insight: Started in 2020 as commerce-specific BI before broadening into a general AI data analyst; raised a $9M Series A led by M13 in 2024.
name: Zenlytic
tagline: AI data analyst that answers business questions in plain language.
description: Zenlytic is a self-serve business intelligence platform whose AI analyst, Zoë, answers natural-language questions by reasoning over a governed semantic layer rather than raw tables, so results map to agreed business definitions. It connects to warehouses like Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, and Databricks plus dbt and Looker semantic models, and returns inspectable analyses, visualizations, and reports inside the app or via Slack and Teams. The emphasis is on auditable, defensible answers for non-technical users.

modelSupport.notes: Vendor-managed LLMs grounded by a semantic layer; not user-selectable.

edge: Grounds its AI analyst in a governed semantic layer, so answers reconcile to existing metric definitions instead of free-form SQL guesses.
pros: Answers checked against a semantic layer
Connects to major warehouses, dbt, and Looker
Delivers analyses in Slack and Teams
cons: Requires a modeled semantic layer to shine
Smaller vendor than incumbent BI suites

references.title: Zenlytic develops commerce-specific, self-serve business intelligence tool
